brief.ask: Direct the premium desktop album view for Plajah Chora (the music service) in the "Cinema" direction, and give three distinct variations of it we can weigh.
brief.surface: Chora album view (PlayerView), desktop 1440×960, dark ground #06040A
brief.domain: music streaming — native Plajah albums and Audius albums open in the same view
brief.audience: listeners who came to play a record, and the artists whose record it is
brief.feeling: premium, impressive, gorgeous — a premiere, not a dashboard
constraints: Cinema layout: the visual viewer (Art / Visualizer / Video / Fullscreen) is a full-bleed hero across the top ~540px; the cover medallion, a very large display title, artist line and one dominant Play sit over its lower edge.

Below the hero: the tracklist (number, title, credits, time) keeps today's behaviour — the playing row carries the purple→magenta gradient, NEXT tag on the queued row, durations in mono, expandable row drawer, bulk select.
Beside the tracklist: synced lyrics, a social card (friends who played it, Listen together / listening party), and Breakdown · Live FX · Comments.

Plajah design language only: purple #6B0099, magenta #D40055, orange #FF8C00 (action), cyan #00DAF3 (live/spatial), lilac #D0BCFF; Bricolage Grotesque display caps, Inter body, JetBrains Mono for time, Newsreader for editorial.
Every existing feature stays reachable: playlist add, offline save, party, back the artist / buy, share & promote, Live FX presets, Pixels, Hide & Seek alternates, comments.
Fewer competing gradients and tiny all-caps labels than today: one primary action, readable type.
references: Current Chora album view: command deck + DSP console stacked above the tracklist
Concept B "Cinema" mockup on the canvas

proposals.title: The Architectural Proscenium and Cantus Firmus
proposals.idea: Anchor the 540px Cinema hero inside a strict 24-column structural bay system where the medallion, display title, and tracklist function as tectonic entablature and columnation over a dark basalt ground.
proposals.geometry: A rigid 24-column cantus firmus grid establishing a 5:3 vertical proportion between the top 540px hero proscenium and the 360px tracklist cellar, with baseline rhythm set at a precise 8px structural module.
proposals.typography: Display titles in Bricolage Grotesque 64px display caps; track credits and editorial commentary in Newsreader 18px italic with generous leading; timecodes in JetBrains Mono 12px; interface navigation in Inter 13px sentence case.
proposals.imageLogic: Generative motion and procedural light constrained strictly within the 540px hero, behaving like light cast across a coffered vault; blend opacity swells from 0.28 to 0.44 only at musical phrase peaks without shifting positional authority.
proposals.texture: Matte basalt #06040A ground layered with procedural 300g cotton vellum tooth, subtle raytraced glass refraction along the cover medallion's rim, and faint intaglio etching lines on key grid intersections.
proposals.motion: Measured architectural pacing: elements do not drift or reconfigure; light swells smoothly across 1.6-second measures tied to the track's bar lines, like sunlight shifting across stone.
proposals.productionMethod: Custom WebGL fragment shaders generating procedural volumetric light rays and glass dispersion seeded from the 24-column grid, executed via React and Three.js with strict CSS Grid baseline alignment.
proposals.humanTrace: The tangible physics of etched printing plates and architectural light—shadows cast at a true 45-degree angle with soft penumbra, conveying the weight of an engraved score.
proposals.risk: Risks appearing solemn or rigid for hyper-pop or fast-paced electronic releases, but earns that weight by treating every album as an enduring theatrical premiere.

arguesWith.why: The Futurist demands a dynamic frame that morphs and reconfigures with audio data; I insist the proscenium frame must remain absolute and fixed so the compositional hierarchy can be read twice the same way.

proposals.title: Heavy Press Offset Cinema
proposals.idea: Treat the 540px hero not as a pristine glass visor, but as a live offset print run pulled under heavy ink pressure, letting dynamic video bleed like wet litho across dark paper tooth.
proposals.geometry: Asymmetrical top hero cut with an unpolished 2px physical separator; tracklist set on a dense 12-column grid with razor-sliced dividers that refuse floaty padding.
proposals.typography: Bricolage Grotesque display caps slammed tight with negative tracking; Newsreader in raw editorial italic for liner notes; JetBrains Mono pinned hard to the right edge; Inter body.
proposals.imageLogic: Generative 16mm silver-halide grain shader dynamic layer; dynamic cyan and magenta color separations shift out of registration during bass peaks to simulate physical press drift.
proposals.texture: Dark #06040A background loaded with high-frequency paper tooth noise; active Play medallion coated in a wet-ink lacquer shader that catches dynamic hero lighting.
proposals.motion: Mechanical inertia; layout elements drop into place like heavy press stamps with zero overshoot easing; lyrics jump on the kick drum with instant physical shutter ticks.
proposals.productionMethod: Custom WebGL fragment shaders applying real-time ink-bleed convolution and procedural registration offset over generative video streams directly in PlayerView.
proposals.humanTrace: Simulated double-pass ink bleed along display letterforms, analog CRT scanline interference, and mechanical registration slip when swapping tracks.
proposals.risk: Risks looking rough to people who equate premium with frictionless glass, but it risks real weight to gain immediate visceral urgency.

arguesWith.why: The Classical Mind wants serene balance and quiet typographic dignity; I want physical pressure, misregistered ink, and visual tension that refuses to settle down.

proposals.title: Volumetric Luminance Spatial Field Engine
proposals.idea: Treat the hero album viewer as a real-time volumetric light instrument that transforms cover artwork and audio stream metrics into physical-plausible spatial refraction and depth.
proposals.geometry: Top 540px hero structured as a 21:9 anamorphic viewport governed by a 24×14 luminance sampling grid; lower body splits into an 8-column tracklist and a 4-column live context rail on a rigid 8px spatial rhythm.
proposals.typography: Bricolage Grotesque in high-contrast display caps for album titles, Inter for body and credits, JetBrains Mono for strict timecode coordinates, and Newsreader for editorial liner notes.
proposals.imageLogic: Generative WebGPU depth-mesh displacement converts two-dimensional artwork into floating volumetric light slabs; live visualizers use procedural ray-marching driven directly by audio FFT frequency bins.
proposals.texture: Procedural micro-lens diffraction, sub-surface light dispersion, simulated glass refraction, and an anti-aliased sensor grain shader modeled after analog ISO 800 film stock.
proposals.motion: Damped spring physics (stiffness 180, damping 12) govern state shifts; sub-bass audio frequencies physically modulate depth-of-field focal planes while queued tracks trigger linear luminance pulses.
proposals.productionMethod: Custom WebGL/WebGPU fragment shaders rendering real-time procedural ray-marching and audio-reactive spatial buffers, eliminating pre-rendered video assets entirely.
proposals.humanTrace: Modeled optical lens aberrations, physically grounded camera micro-drift, and real-time depth-of-field blur based on calculated physical aperture stops.
proposals.risk: Demands WebGPU processing capability on the client client-side; worth the trade-off because it turns a static video header into an active, responsive spatial instrument.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist demands stage curtains and visual reveals, whereas I require continuous visual behavior derived strictly from the music input signal.

proposals.title: Archival Topography and Living Provenance
proposals.idea: Frame the Cinema visualizer as a real-time procedural film contact sheet and topographic field survey, seeding visualizer geometry directly from the album's recording coordinates rather than abstract digital noise.
proposals.geometry: A 540px hero built on a 5-axis cartographic grid anchored by coordinate notch margins, transitioning into a dual-column ledger below with strict 24px baseline intervals and precise 48px row heights for the tracklist.
proposals.typography: Bricolage Grotesque display caps for album titles, paired with Newsreader italic for place-based liner notes, Inter for crisp track metadata, and JetBrains Mono for latitude-style duration indexes.
proposals.imageLogic: Procedural WebGL shader simulating 35mm film halation and Kodachrome color response curves; audio spectrum data drives real-time topographic height-field contours calculated from the artist's named recording latitude.
proposals.texture: Tactile procedural fiber weave simulating 120gsm unbleached field notebook paper in shadow zones, layered over dark obsidian ground #06040A with subtle optical lens vignetting.
proposals.motion: Unhurried 60fps pan across topographic contour vectors, with track transitions executed via a 1.2-second optical shutter fade mimicking analog film transport inertia.
proposals.productionMethod: Real-time WebGL/GLSL fragment shaders computing spectral contour topographies, organic film halation, and paper tooth entirely on the GPU via procedural code.
proposals.humanTrace: Physical film grain density shifts derived from historic documentary stocks, accompanied by simulated hand-inked margin register marks in tracklist drawers.
proposals.risk: Risks feeling dense or archival to users accustomed to sterile tech dashboards, but this grounding transforms a streaming view into a reverent cultural premiere.

arguesWith.why: The Futurist treats visualizer code as an origin-free abstraction; I insist that generative seeds be bound to real-world coordinates and physical film physics so novelty never erases provenance.
